clue.text: Sing like Antonio forswearing the alien sea

indicators.note: to forswear is to renounce or give up, so the sea's word is dropped from the trader's title

parts.note: Antonio is the title character of Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, so to be like him is to be a merchant
mer is the French word for sea, a foreign or alien term

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean singer imitates Antonio while swearing off the strange ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forswearing' removes MER, French for sea, from the front of MERCHANT, leaving CHANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To chant is to sing or intone words rhythmically, as in church plainsong.

clue.text: Sort of oracle apt for an old queen

indicators.note: sort of signals that the letters are sorted into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An ancient queen finds a kind of prophet suitable for her.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra was the last ruler of ancient Egypt, a famous queen of antiquity.

clue.text: A chain derived from a Trojan design

indicators.note: derived from means the letters are drawn out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A necklace was copied from an ancient Trojan pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are the mountain chain running down western South America.

clue.text: Likely spot for fortune-tellers in China

definitions.text: Likely spot for fortune-tellers in China

parts.words: Likely spot for fortune-tellers in China
parts.note: fortunes are read in leftover leaves in a cup, and a Chinese café serving the drink would be the natural place

explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese café for drinking brews is where readers of leaves in the cup would naturally gather.

clue.text: Wild animals rub against trees

parts.note: to buff is to rub or polish a surface
aloes are plants, some of them tree-like, as the aloe tree

explanation.surface: Beasts in the wild scratch themselves on tree trunks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' simply sets the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Buffaloes are large wild oxen, roaming beasts of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Satisfactory Big Bang

definitions.meaning: ... as slang adjective for prosperous, going well
a loud deep explosion

explanation.definitionFit: A boom is a loud explosive sound and a period of thriving trade, when things go well.

clue.text: Sheriff's conclusion given in full, loud and clear

definitions.text: Sheriff's conclusion given in full, loud and clear

parts.words: Sheriff's conclusion given in full, loud and clear
parts.note: the last two letters of the word sheriff are ff, the musical marking for very loud, here spelt out as a full Italian word

explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical term means very loud, and its abbreviation ff ends the word sheriff.

clue.text: Wellesley dubbed by the King

definitions.meaning: ... Wellesley, Duke of Wellington, was so named at baptism
the legendary British ruler of Camelot

explanation.definitionFit: Arthur was the first name of Wellesley, Duke of Wellington, and of the legendary ruler of Camelot.

clue.text: Banner seen from a mile off

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are thrown out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A flag is spotted a long way away.
explanation.definitionFit: The oriflamme was the red-gold standard of the French kings, a battle flag.

clue.text: Witticism from Carey's girl

definitions.meaning: a witty remark or quip
Henry Carey wrote the song ... in Our Alley about his sweetheart

explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a quick witty retort, and Sally is the girl of Henry Carey's song.

clue.text: Cook's craft is to have a go

definitions.meaning: Captain James Cook's ship on his first Pacific voyage
to try or attempt something

explanation.definitionFit: HMS Endeavour was Captain Cook's famous vessel, and to endeavour is to make an attempt.

clue.text: Dry run for an examination

definitions.meaning: a rehearsal or test run before the real thing
a judicial hearing in court, or a test of ability

explanation.definitionFit: A trial is both a practice test and a court hearing that examines a case.

clue.text: Ancient means of shooting someone

definitions.meaning: Ancient ... is Falstaff's swaggering ensign in Shakespeare; ancient was the old word for an ensign
a handgun

explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Pistol is the Shakespearean ensign, and a pistol is a handgun for firing at someone.

clue.text: How belief is confirmed

parts.note: the proverb 'seeing is believing' says that faith comes from what the eyes witness

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means by sight, and the proverb holds that sight is what makes people believe.

clue.text: Needed after first blow to fight back?

definitions.text: Needed after first blow to fight back?

parts.words: Needed after first blow to fight back?
parts.note: a boxer knocked breathless recovers his breathing to carry on; blow is read as a gasp of breath

explanation.definitionFit: Renewed energy after exhaustion is a revival of breath that lets one carry on.

clue.text: Bridge is about partners at cross purposes?

indicators.note: the word for bridge goes about, or around, the partners, enclosing them

parts.note: to traverse is to cross over, as a bridge does
North and South are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A bridge player complains that partners keep misunderstanding each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' looks like the card game, which 'partners' supports, but it is the verb to span; bridge supplies NS (North and South) instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Transverse means lying crosswise, so it serves for 'cross' purposes in a playful sense.

clue.text: Philosopher has a drink outside to sort it out.

indicators.note: outside means the drink goes around the rearranged letters

parts.note: ale is a drink

indicators.note: sort it out means the letters are sorted into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A thinker reaches for a beer in order to solve a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a drink' is ALE here, and the surface's 'to sort it out' hides the anagram: 'out' is the signal working on 'sort it', with 'to' a mere link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the Greek thinker who tutored Alexander the Great.

clue.text: Give out the enemy is returning

indicators.note: returning means the word for the enemy is read backwards

parts.note: time is often called 'the enemy', as in the phrase 'time is the enemy'

explanation.surface: A sentry reports that the foe is coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is returning' turns TIME round to EMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or discharge, as light or sound.

clue.text: Temple too, unorthodox for an Indian set-up

indicators.note: unorthodox suggests the letters are set out in an irregular order

explanation.surface: A religious building that is unconventional too, built for a Native American community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unorthodox' rearranges TEMPLETOO; 'Indian' is the old term for Native American.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved post erected by Native American peoples, so something set up by them.

clue.text: Sheriff's company commander calls a carriage

definitions.meaning: the captain leading the company in R. C. Sherriff's First World War play Journey's End
a light open horse-drawn gig named after the clergyman Fitzroy who first had one built

explanation.definitionFit: Stanhope is the officer leading the men in Sherriff's Journey's End, and also a light horse-drawn gig.

clue.text: A number back alliance

indicators.note: back means the number's word is read in reverse

parts.note: six is a number

explanation.surface: A count of members takes us back to some old coalition.
explanation.walkthrough: X is the Roman numeral ten, but here 'number' is the word SIX, which 'back' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Axis was the wartime alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan; an axis is also any pact between states.

clue.text: Entrust people with their first duty

parts.note: to commit something is to entrust it to someone's care
men means people

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of the word their

explanation.surface: Hand responsibility to staff along with their main obligation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives T from 'their', closing the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: A commitment is an obligation or pledge one is bound to honour.

clue.text: Essayist an example of strength to note

parts.note: steel is proverbially strong, a byword for toughness
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A writer gives an instance of fortitude for us to record.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Steele co-founded The Spectator and was a celebrated writer of short prose pieces.

clue.text: Puck could have quickly described such a line

definitions.text: Puck could have quickly described such a line

parts.words: Puck could have quickly described such a line
parts.note: in A Midsummer Night's Dream Puck boasts he will put a girdle round about the earth in forty minutes, tracing a circle parallel to the equator

explanation.definitionFit: A line of latitude is a circle round the globe, the girdle that Puck promised to put round the earth.

clue.text: Ease possibility of having to move on?

definitions.meaning: a slackening or lessening

definitions.text: possibility of having to move on?
definitions.meaning: read as two words, a rental agreement that has run out, so the tenant may have to leave

explanation.definitionFit: A let-up is a lull or easing, and when a rental lease is up the tenant may need to leave.

clue.text: Shaky but evidently still employed

definitions.meaning: weak or unsteady through age or illness
read as two words, ..., still working for a company

explanation.definitionFit: Infirm means feeble or unsteady, while split as two words it says someone remains at a company.

clue.text: Man is one of these, despite Donne

definitions.text: Man is one of these, despite Donne

parts.words: Man is one of these, despite Donne
parts.note: John Donne wrote 'No man is an island', yet the Isle of Man is one

explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea, contrary to Donne's line that no man is one.

clue.text: "And gentlemen in England, now ______" (Hen. V)

parts.note: the St Crispin's Day speech in Shakespeare's Henry V says those gentlemen still in their beds at home will think themselves accursed

explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in King Henry's Agincourt speech means in bed, sleeping safely at home.

clue.text: Heading for example Westward Ho!

definitions.meaning: a caption at the top of a page or chapter
Westward Ho! is the name of a Charles Kingsley novel, so it is a book's name

explanation.definitionFit: A title is a heading, and Westward Ho! is the name of a novel by Charles Kingsley.

clue.text: Explosion in oil rig, with mob in confusion

indicators.note: an explosion blows the letters apart so they land in a new order

explanation.surface: A blast on an oil platform sends a crowd into chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosion in' rearranges OILRIG and MOB into IMBROGLIO.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is an entangled, chaotic situation or muddle.

clue.text: Make-believe taken care of in advance

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before or in advance
tended means looked after

explanation.surface: A nanny's pretend game was all prepared beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the clue in reverse order; 'in advance' naturally stands in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretended means feigned or imaginary, as in a make-believe game.

clue.text: Result from University points structure

indicators.note: structure means the letters are built into a new arrangement

parts.note: E, N, S and E are compass points

explanation.surface: A ranking comes out of a university's scoring scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'structure' rearranges U with the points ENSE into ENSUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow as a consequence, to come about afterwards.
